target.title: fix: improve publisher abuse scan resilience
target.body:
## Summary

Publisher-abuse pressure scoring was spending most of its runtime asleep between continuation actions. The cron processed 5 pages of 250 publishers, then waited 60 seconds before the next continuation, which adds roughly 6 hours of scheduler idle time for a ~475k-publisher run before counting the actual scoring work.

This keeps the existing serial cursor-based scan design, but makes the continuation cadence match the work: 20 pages per action, the same 250-publisher mutation page size, and a 5-second delay between score-run continuations. It also adds bounded retry/resume for transient Convex failures so a long run does not fail permanently on a single generic platform retry error or run-doc OCC failure.

## What Changed

- Pressure score cron throughput: runs `maxPages: 20` instead of `5`, so each action can process up to 5,000 publishers while each mutation still only handles 250 publishers.
- Pressure score continuation delay: score-run continuations now wait 5 seconds instead of sharing the generic 60-second action delay used by other workflows.
- Bounded transient retries: generic Convex transient errors and `changed while this mutation was being run` now record telemetry and reschedule the same run with exponential backoff from 30 seconds to 5 minutes, capped at 5 retry attempts.
- Observability: score-run docs now record transient error count, last transient error, last transient error time, and next retry time; the action also logs retry and exhausted-budget events.
- Failure semantics: deterministic page failures still mark the score run failed, and exhausted transient retries also fail the run instead of looping forever.

## Proof

Read-only production investigation found the bottleneck and failure class:

- Convex insights for production showed `publisherAbuse.js:collectPublisherAbuseScoresPageInternal` OCC retries on the `publishers` table, not publisher-abuse read/byte limit failures.
- Current batching was 1,250 publishers per action followed by 60 seconds of idle delay. At ~475,000 publishers, that creates about 380 continuations and about 6.3 hours of scheduler delay alone.
- Keeping the 250-publisher mutation page avoids increasing individual transaction read/write pressure while reducing continuation idle time to about 95 continuations and under 8 minutes of scheduled delay for the same corpus size.
- Parallel sharding is intentionally not part of this PR: the current pressure model accumulates `sumLogPressure` and `sumSquaredLogPressure` during collection, then finalizes scores by ordered cursor/rank. Sharding that safely would require a separate aggregation/ranking design, not a small resilience fix.

No screenshot is included because this is backend-only cron/action/schema behavior; the management UI surface is unchanged.

## Verification

Reviewer-checkable behavior:

- The cron now schedules pressure scoring with `batchSize: 250`, `maxPages: 20`, `trigger: "cron"`.
- A retryable collection failure records transient telemetry and schedules the same run after 30 seconds without marking it failed.
- A retryable collection failure at `retryAttempt: 5` marks the run failed and does not schedule another retry.
- A normal incomplete score-run action schedules its continuation after 5 seconds.

Automated checks run locally:

- `bun run format convex/publisherAbuse.ts convex/publisherAbuse.test.ts convex/crons.ts convex/crons.test.ts convex/schema.ts`
- `bunx vitest run convex/publisherAbuse.test.ts convex/crons.test.ts`
- `bunx tsc --noEmit --pretty false`
- `bunx convex codegen --typecheck=disable`
- `git diff --check`
- `bun run ci:static`
- `bun run ci:unit`
- `bun run ci:types-build` passed after removing ignored build output from a first run that hit local `ENOSPC` during Nitro asset copy.

Not completed:

- Structured autoreview: local reviewer engines were blocked by authentication/workspace policy before returning review findings.
